session_covered: US and European sessions of Monday 5 October
intro: Covers the US session of Monday 5 October. Sourcing caveat: several figures could not be verified as official closes or conflicted between sources and are marked "not available"; Tuesday-morning SPI 200 futures could not be sourced.
footnotes: NASDAQ Composite: approximate figure (the email gave "~27,403.57 pts (record) +0.7%").
US 10-year Treasury yield: approximate figure (the email gave "~5.33% ~+5bp").

S&P 500 and Nasdaq are Trading Economics' latest figures and could not be confirmed as official closes (intraday gains of +0.6% to +0.7% were reported elsewhere). Dow omitted: sources disagreed on direction. 10-year yield ~5.33% (Trading Economics; another source 5.34%) versus Friday's 5.28%, so the ~+5bp change is derived. Brent (US$99.93/bbl -2.27% vs US$102.90/bbl +0.64%) and gold (+0.65% vs -0.17%) conflicted between sources and could not be reconciled. Iron ore: another source cites US$90.90/t.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures for this morning: not available. The only futures quote found was a stale Monday day-session close (8,745.5, +0.78%) and is not used. Wall Street's tech-led gains point to a firmer start, but no implied open is given. The ASX 200 closed Monday at about 8,691–8,692 (+0.04% to +0.10%) in a quiet session with a NSW public holiday.

what_moved: Technology and communication services led US equities, with the Nasdaq at a record, as Friday's weak September payrolls (+29,000 vs 90,000 expected) cut Fed rate-hike odds. Yields nonetheless rose: the 10-year held around 5.3% and the 30-year about 5.7%. ISM services slowed to 54.9 from 55.4. Sector percentages are not available.

news.headline: Weak jobs, higher yields.
news.summary: Payrolls of 29,000 failed to pull yields lower; heavy Treasury supply and energy-driven inflation risk are cited as reasons.

news.headline: US services growth eases.
news.summary: ISM services slipped to 54.9 in September from 55.4 in August.

news.headline: Euro-area bond stress.
news.summary: The French–German 10-year spread is at 141bp, the widest since 2012.

news.headline: Iron ore stays weak.
news.summary: About US$91/t, down roughly 8.6% over the past month.

news.headline: AUD near multi-month lows.
news.summary: AUD/USD 0.6938 on a firmer US dollar and high Treasury yields; the RBA cash rate is 4.6% after a September hike.

news.headline: Firmus IPO priced.
news.summary: The AI data-centre operator priced at A$11 a share, valuing it at about A$43.7bn.

coming_up: Wednesday 7 October (US): 10-year Treasury auction (1pm ET) followed by September FOMC minutes (2pm ET). Thursday 8 October: 30-year reopening.
